reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes Al2O3 nanoparticle formation and strength enhancement in a completely different material system (NiAl-HEA composites processed by MA and SPS), not in cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38. It provides no support for the key premises regarding dispersion method, crack-blunting mechanism, preservation of caloric response, or the specific strength target in the proposed alloy.
premises: Nanocrystalline Al2O3 particles can be uniformly dispersed in a cast alloy matrix via ultrasonic-assisted melt stirring
Al2O3 nanoparticles at grain boundaries and within the matrix act as obstacles to crack propagation, enhancing toughness and compressive strength
The continuous crystalline matrix maintains the magnetostructural transition necessary for the caloric effect despite nanoparticle addition
A 1–3 vol% Al2O3 addition can raise compressive strength to >220 MPa in the target alloy
